name: Neodymium magnets
summary: Neodymium (rare earth) magnets: small, silver and extremely strong.
uses: Building efficient wind and water generators
Triggering reed switches and Hall sensors
Fishing metal out of water or debris
identify: Shiny silver or nickel-plated pieces: curved pairs on steel plates inside hard drives, small discs in phones, earbuds and speakers, and arcs in brushless motors, hub motors and cordless tools.
test: They grab steel hard from a distance; neodymium weakens above about 80 °C, so heated ones may be weak. Big ones pinch skin and shatter into sharp chips; keep them away from pacemakers and electronics.
